text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication in the angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) class used to treat high blood pressure, protect the kidneys in type 2 diabetes, and lower the risk of stroke.
These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position)
Upper respiratory tract infections (such as a stuffy or runny nose, or sore throat)
Digestive issues (nausea, diarrhea, or mild stomach upset)
Back or joint pain and muscle cramps

text_blocks.snippet: Contact your doctor or seek emergency care right away if you experience:

list.snippet: Allergic reactions / Angioedema: Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, eyes, hands, or feet, or difficulty breathing or swallowing (a medical emergency).
High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, numbness or tingling, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
Low blood pressure (hypotension): Severe dizziness, fainting, or blurry vision.
Kidney problems: A major decrease in the amount of urine, blood in the urine, or unexplained swelling in the legs, ankles, or hands.
Liver issues: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or severe upper stomach pain.
Stand up slowly: To prevent dizziness or fainting spells when getting out of bed or a chair, transition slowly.
Avoid potassium supplements: Do not use potassium-containing salt substitutes or supplements unless directed by your healthcare provider, as losartan can raise potassium levels.
Pregnancy warning: Losartan should not be taken during pregnancy, as it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby.
